title: prefill + decode pipeline: chunked prefill, speculative prefill, stage-overlap + kernel scheduler improvements
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Reduce end-to-end inference latency and improve GPU utilization for mixed prefill+decode workloads. This PR targets three related optimizations: (1) chunked prefill (split long prefill sequences into cacheable chunks and overlap compute), (2) speculative prefill for common prefixes to reduce decode stalls when KV cache warmup is slow, and (3) stage-overlap decoding where prefill, kernel scheduling and decode stages can run concurrently across micro-batches. The changes also introduce a small kernel scheduler that prefers precompiled kernels based on recent sequence-length distribution to reduce kernel launch overhead and improve L2 cache locality.

Summary of changes: Implement chunked prefill path in serving/runtime/prefill, add speculative prefill heuristic and metrics, extend continuous-batching scheduler to support stage overlap, add kernel selection table with eviction policy, wire KV-cache warmup hooks to the scheduler, and add end-to-end tests and benchmarks.

Checklist:
- [x] Chunked prefill implementation + unit tests
- [x] Speculative prefill heuristic + opt-in config flag
- [x] Stage-overlap orchestration in batch scheduler
- [x] Kernel scheduler with lightweight telemetry
- [x] Integration tests covering KV cache correctness and fallback
- [x] Benchmarks and perf dashboards updated

Notes on behavior and compatibility: Default behavior is opt-in behind runtime flag `enable_prefill_decode_overlap` and `speculative_prefill_threshold_ms`. No incompatibility to user API. Kernel scheduler is a local heuristic and can be disabled via `kernel_scheduler.enabled=false` for deterministic debugging.

Related work: follows design in ENG-2381 (prefill chunking RFC) and ENG-2420 (scheduler revamp). See earlier prefill-stage-overlap PRs for performance comparisons (references: PRs 40621, 42342, 45210).
commit_summary: feat(prefill): add chunked prefill path and tests; feat(scheduler): stage-overlap orchestration + continuous batching updates; perf(kernel): kernel selection table and heuristic; feat(kv-cache): warmup hooks and metrics; test: add integration + perf harness updates; docs: runtime flags and release notes
patch_highlights: serving/runtime/prefill/chunked_prefill.cpp: new prefill loop that emits KV chunks for downstream decode; maintains per-request chunk metadata and alignment with KV cache slots
serving/runtime/scheduler/continuous_batch_scheduler.cpp: add pipeline stages (PREFILL, KERNEL_SCHEDULE, DECODE) and state machine to allow overlapping stages across micro-batches
serving/runtime/scheduler/kernel_scheduler.cpp: small LRU table mapping (model, seq_len_range) -> preferred kernel id + run_count heuristic
serving/runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache_manager.cpp: expose warmup_async(request_id) hook and metrics (kv_warmup_latency_ms, kv_warmup_hits)
serving/tests/prefill_integration_test.cpp: cover correctness for chunk boundary cases and speculative prefill fallback when cache misses occur
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Overall this looks promising. A few concerns: the speculative prefill path can add extra GPU work—can you add a guard to limit speculative effort per-socket? Also please add a perf test for very short responses where overhead could regress.
Priya Nair (author): Added `speculative_prefill.max_extra_tokens_per_batch` and a perf test for short responses. See benchmark updates in benchmarks/prefill_decode_overlap_bench.py.
Aisha Khan: Kernel scheduler seems lightweight but we need metrics for cold-start mispredictions. Can you emit kernel_chooser.hits/misses with labels?
Priya Nair: Added kernel_chooser.hits and kernel_chooser.misses counters and a debug flag to log evictions. Also added unit tests for eviction behavior.
Liam O'Connor: CI flake in perf benchmark job previously; re-running. Also verify that disabling kernel_scheduler reproduces previous scheduling behavior exactly.
Priya Nair: Verified in local tests; added an e2e scenario that toggles kernel_scheduler and asserts identical results for deterministic models in test harness.
ci_checks: unit-tests: passed (including new prefill unit tests)
perf_results_summary: Observed 12-18% lower p99 latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads with long prefixes (seq_len>1024) on A100; 7-10% GPU utilization improvement in 8x concurrent stream scenarios. Short-response (<32 tokens) microbenchmarks show <2% regression when kernel_scheduler disabled; enabling scheduler recovers ~1.5% improvement.
fallback_and_safety: Speculative prefill is gated and will be disabled if kv_warmup_latency_ms > spec_prefill_max_latency_ms. If any KV cache inconsistencies are detected during integration tests, requests fall back to the safe decode path (no chunking).
merge_details: squash and merge by Aisha Khan. Commit message summarises chunked prefill, scheduler and kernel chooser changes. Changelist annotated for release v1.12.0-rc1
release_notes:
- Add chunked prefill to reduce KV warmup stalls and enable overlapping prefill+decode stages.
- Introduce speculative prefill heuristic to reduce early-decode latency for common prefixes (opt-in).
- Add lightweight kernel scheduler to prefer warmed kernels based on recent seq-length patterns.
- New runtime flags to control overlap, speculation, and kernel scheduler behavior.
- Performance: p99 improvements on long-prefix workloads; opt-in flags for safe rollout.
post_merge_actions: - Rollout: enable `enable_prefill_decode_overlap` for canary fleet (10%) and monitor kv_warmup_latency_ms and end-to-end p99.\n- Add dashboard widgets: kernel_chooser.hits/misses, kv_warmup_latency_ms, speculative_prefill.attempts/successes.\n- Follow-up: ENG-2484 to evaluate per-model kernel tables and persistence.
